investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. The pod remained unscheduled for ~140–148 seconds before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and failing every contract assertion.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules. With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod creation attempt fails immediately with Unschedulable, preventing the eval runner from reaching the agent creation step and producing any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

TERTIARY — Cluster-level resource quota or LimitRange for kata.peerpods.io/vm set too low for concurrent eval probes: if multiple eval runs or production workloads compete for the same VM slots simultaneously, the quota ceiling may be hit transiently.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required confidential-compute pods: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector. No preemption victims were available, so every pod remained Unschedulable for 140–148 seconds before the eval timed out and returned empty evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes. When the eval runner called createAgent with type "remote" (source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918), the resulting pod could not be scheduled because 0/6 nodes were available: 2 had Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The pod remained Unschedulable for the full eval window, so no agent was ever created, no runtime response was obtained, and all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were absent from the eval result. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool in production-api; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader user-facing outage.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource pool is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or a previous eval run's leaked agents are holding all VM slots, leaving none available for new probe pods.

Secondary — a previous eval run's remote agent pods were not cleaned up (withCleanup path in run-status-probes.mjs may have failed or been interrupted), leaving VM slots occupied and preventing new scheduling.

Tertiary — the cluster's kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool has been scaled down or a node has become NotReady, reducing available capacity from its expected level to the point where concurrent demand exceeds supply.

Quaternary — the pod's node affinity/selector is misconfigured or has drifted such that only 2 nodes are eligible instead of a larger set, making the pool more susceptible to exhaustion under normal load.
